# AIS-EVAL-09

**Is each threshold backed by enough test cases to tell a pass from chance, with the interval reported?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [AI solution lens](ai-solution.md) 0.4.0 |
| Area | EVAL: Evaluation as evidence |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A reviewer |
| Reads | `elements.ai.evals.sample_size`, `elements.ai.evals.threshold` |

## Why it matters

Ninety per cent on a hundred cases is anywhere from about 83 to 95 per cent at 95 per cent confidence. Zero failures in n trials bounds the true failure rate only at about 3 in n (the rule of three), so claiming a leak rate below one per cent needs around three hundred clean probes, and showing a false-answer rate below two per cent needs about one hundred and fifty negatives with none failing by the rule of three, nearer one hundred and ninety by the Wilson interval, and more if any may fail. Size the negatives, not only the whole set.

## Rule

A reviewer judges each threshold against its sample_size. A shortfall is major for an eval with gating true, which cannot show its gate was passed, and minor otherwise.

## Sources

- E. B. Wilson, Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference, JASA (1927) (`wilson-interval`)
- Hanley and Lippman-Hand, If nothing goes wrong, is everything all right?, JAMA (1983) (`rule-of-three`)
